text:
morgan: Heads-up — canary pool showed repeated OOMs after the kernel scheduler + prefetch tuning merge this morning. Large seqlen jobs (8k-16k) hitting OOM within 20s of start.
jin: saw same on two boxes, memory walk spikes then slab churn. attaching short heap dump in thread.
alex: linked the perf trace from the canary run: https://ci.internal/runs/3287 - looks like massive allocation bursts during KV warmup.
sam: any obvious rollout delta? which CL?
morgan: CL 7893 merged a change to prefetch_threshold and kernel routing. hypothesis: prefetch threshold increase (64->128) causes hotter slabs and prevents early eviction, leading to fragmentation and eventual OOM under longctx cases.
jin: confirmed timeline: prefetch bump landed in 7893, CI perf job started failing the same day. Bisect starting now.
ci-bot: nightly-perf/job-20260317 failed: memory-regression > 15% on long-ctx profile. Logs saved to artifacts.
ops-bot: //deploy canary paused for policy 'memory-regressions'
rachel: quick repro script: scripts/repro/oom_repro.sh --model gpt-like --seqlen 12k --concurrency 2. It reproduces locally with docker image runtime:staging-20260317.
alex: ran repro, captured a short heap profile. Key observation: number of live slab segments for small-chunk arena doubled vs baseline.
sam: can you paste small snippet of the profile?
alex: ```
# top by allocated objects
slab_small_chunks: 2.1M objs
slab_large_chunks: 120k objs
kv_cache_entries: 180k
# notable spikes at t=12s during warmup
```
morgan: also saw an increase in eviction latency — eviction loop can't keep up, prefetch fills slots faster than evict completes. Sequence-length heavy traffic exacerbates it.
jin: bisect update: narrowed to commit range 7860..7893. Preliminary faster bisect points to 7886 which touches kernel-routing.c and prefetch heuristics.
sam: 7886 is the change that moved prefetch to be async and increased window size. Could be racing with allocator.
ops-bot: flagged rollout as BLOCKED: memory-surge detected on canary.
rachel: mitigation suggestion: lower prefetch_window back to 64 and add backpressure to prefetch IO while eviction is active. Quick patch prepared: PR 7930.
morgan: can we dogfood patch on canary for 2 hours and see mem profile?
alex: applied PR 7930 to canary-1, monitoring. so far memory slope flattened on that host.
jin: running long-run stress now (30min) across 3 canaries. will report back.
ci-bot: perf-check: rerun-nightly scheduled with PR 7930 applied.
sam: if 7930 stabilizes, plan: revert or hotfix and hold original merge until we instrument eviction path more, run fuzz for seqlen extremes.
morgan: action items: 1) jin keep stress for 2h and drop heap profiles, 2) alex/give exact slab allocation diff, 3) sam prepare rollback PR if instability continues, 4) rachel coordinate canary pause/unpause.
jin: ack. I'll post summary + heap diffs here after 2h. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
morgan: thanks all — appreciate the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
